study_identification_part.si4_title: Individual-level deviations from normative brain morphology in violence, psychosis, and psychopathy

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract clearly states the study aims: to use normative modeling to explore individual-level brain heterogeneity, quantify individual deviations, compare group differences among SSD-V, SSD-NV, nonSSD-V, and HC, and examine associations with psychopathy traits.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: We explored brain heterogeneity in persons ... from lifetime normative trajectories of cortical thickness, surface area, and subcortical volumes. Normative models ... were used to investigate individual deviances, group differences, and associations to psychopathy traits.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: An EXISTING normative model was used and cited. A local unmatched healthy control set (n=998) was used for site-specific fine-tuning (recalibration). Eligibility for the local healthy sample is described (no neurological or severe mental disorders; age ranges per study). Image quality control procedures and exclusion reasons are detailed (MRIQC screening, visual QC; exclusions for poor quality and spurious findings). Final sample sizes for groups and the calibration HC set are reported.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: We used pretrained normative models from https://github.com/predictiveclinical-neuroscience/braincharts ... data of 58835 individuals ... An unmatched group of healthy controls ( n = 998) was utilized to fine-tune model parameters ... Healthy participants were ... The inclusion criteria were ... no history of neurological or severe mental disorders. Image quality checking was carried out in two steps. First, all T1w images were processed using MRIqc ... Then two trained raters visually examined the scans ... 52 males and 20 females were excluded due to insufficient T1w image quality, and 3 additional male individuals were excluded due to spurious abnormal brain findings.

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and scanner (site) are explicitly included as covariates in the normative model, and site effects are further addressed via fine-tuning with local HC. Sex is not stated as a covariate in the model description.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: ... the independent variables were age and scanner. ... An unmatched group of healthy controls ( n = 998) was utilized to fine-tune model parameters, enabling the application of normative models to unseen sites.

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The study specifies that pretrained models from the braincharts project were used, trained on 58,835 individuals from 82 sites, and provides the repository URL.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: We used pretrained normative models from https://github.com/predictiveclinical-neuroscience/braincharts. Briefly, models were trained using data of 58835 individuals aged 2-100 from 82 sites.

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: The study applies an EXISTING normative model; per guidance, image acquisition protocol for the reference cohort is not applicable.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing and quality control are described: automated MRIQC screening followed by visual QC, processing in FreeSurfer v7.1, cortical parcellation with Destrieux atlas, and subcortical segmentation per standard atlas.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: Image quality checking was carried out in two steps. First, all T1w images were processed using MRIqc ... Then two trained raters visually examined the scans ... FreeSurfer v7.1 was used to process data that passed quality control. Cortical thickness and area was summarized using the Destrieux atlas parcellation scheme. Subcortical volume segmentation was based on a probabilistic atlas with priors for 31 brain structures.

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: An EXISTING normative model was used; internal data partitioning for model development is not applicable per guidance.

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: An EXISTING normative model was used; external validation on independent healthy datasets for a newly built model is not applicable.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The study did not build a NEW normative model but applied pretrained models; per guidance, detailed modeling approach reporting for newly trained models is not applicable.

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Model performance metrics for a NEW model are not applicable because pretrained normative models were used.

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No new model training or data partitioning for the reference cohort was performed; pretrained models were applied.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: The source of the normative model is provided (GitHub repository), and software versions for application are specified (Python 3.8, PCNtoolkit v0.20).
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: We used pretrained normative models from https://github.com/predictiveclinical-neuroscience/braincharts ... Models were both trained and applied to our data using python 3.8 and PCNtoolkit package (version 0.20).

Final group sample sizes are reported.

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses include clinical covariates beyond demographics in specific models (e.g., PCL-R psychopathy scores and psychosis status in GLM of deviation scores). Matching and GLMs control for age and scanner, and ICV for area/volume. However, broader clinical covariates such as medication status or illness duration are not incorporated as covariates in the main deviation analyses.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: The R package matchIt was used to match age and scanning sites ... GLM ... controlling for the effects of age ... additionally ... included intracranial volume (ICV). ... to examine the association between PCL-R scores and deviation scores ... PCL-R total score, age, psychosis status, and ICV ... were included as independent variables.

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: Primary data collection sources are specified: four Oslo-area studies (TOP, STROKEMRI, uTOP, sTOP).
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: Participants ... were recruited from the Oslo area as part of four studies: the Thematically Organized Psychosis study (TOP) ... the STROKEMRI study ... The Youth-TOP study (uTOP) ... and The Forensic Psychiatry study (sTOP).

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes per group are reported; demographic and clinical characteristics are summarized with differences noted (age, IQ, DUDIT; no differences in AUDIT and PANSS).
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: The remaining participants consisted of four groups ... SSD-V, n = 38 ... nonSSD-V, n = 20 ... SSD-NV n = 138 ... HC, n = 196 ... Demographic characteristics are summarized in Table 1. Groups differed significantly on age, IQ score, and substance use (DUDIT), but not in alcohol use (AUDIT) and PANSS scores.

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Clinical measures and assessment procedures are specified, including structured diagnostic interviews (SCID-I, K-SADS), psychosis symptoms (PANSS), IQ (WASI), substance use (AUDIT, DUDIT), psychopathy (PCL-R), and mental disorders screening in HC (PRIME-MD).
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: Structured diagnostic assessment was performed with the SCID-I ... and the KIDDIE-SADS ... The positive and negative symptom scale (PANSS) ... WASI for IQ ... AUDIT and DUDIT ... Psychopathy traits were assessed with the Psychopathy Checklist Revised (PCL-R) ... The HC were assessed for mental disorders using the Primary Care Evaluation of Mental Disorders.

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The study defines deviation scores, distinguishes positive and negative values, and uses explicit thresholds (|Z|>2) to define extreme deviations and compare frequencies. Broader clinical implications are discussed at a high level, but detailed interpretation of direction and magnitude per ROI in clinical terms is limited.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: ... we computed deviation scores (Z-scores) by separating them into positive and negative deviations. The percentage ... with extreme positive (Z > 2) and negative (Z < -2) deviations ...
